numerical_failure.observed_behavior: For pathological inputs, np.random.zipf hangs indefinitely and does not respond to Ctrl+C (interpreter appears to hang forever). For inputs very close to 1, np.random.zipf hangs for a possibly finite but very long time, also not responding to Ctrl+C.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: For np.random.zipf(np.nan), it should probably just throw an exception. For a near 1 (e.g., 1.0000000000001), the long delays/hangs should be fixed; the issue reports that this was addressed by changing the legacy zipf implementation to model a Zipf distribution truncated to RAND_INT_MAX using rejection that rejects out-of-range/overflow candidates.
trigger_conditions: a is very close to 1 (e.g., np.random.zipf(1.0000000000001))

internally, in the legacy implementation’s rejection sampling, candidate X can exceed (double)RAND_INT_MAX, be rejected, and this can happen extremely often when a is close to 1, causing very long delays/hangs
internally, when U is sufficiently small and a is close to 1, X may overflow to infinity, increasing rejection probability

oracle_clues: The bug is described as an interpreter hang for np.random.zipf(np.nan) and a very long hang for np.random.zipf(1.0000000000001).
Expected behavior for NaN: “should probably just throw an exception.”

The proposed/implemented fix rationale: when a is close to 1, 1/(a-1) is large; with small U, X can exceed RAND_INT_MAX or overflow to infinity; this causes the rejection loop to spend a lot of time rejecting values, leading to long delays/hangs.
The fix models a Zipf distribution truncated to sys.maxint and rejects values where X > (double)RAND_INT_MAX or X < 1.0.

numerical_characteristics.magnitude: truncated to signed 64 bit integers / RAND_INT_MAX (sys.maxint)
category_specific_evidence: The issue is reported as: calling `np.random.zipf(1.0000000000001)` “hangs for a possibly finite but very long time, also not responding to Ctrl+C”.
Regression test comment: “Regression test for gh-9829: a call such as rng.zipf(1.0000000000001) would hang.”
Test uses `n = 100000` and asserts `np.count_nonzero(sample < 2**62) > n/2` after calling `self.mt19937.zipf(1.0000000000001, size=n)`.
PR description explains the rejection sampling loop: candidate `X = floor(pow(U, -1.0 / am1))` where `am1 = a - 1.0`, with rejection when `X > (double)RAND_INT_MAX || X < 1.0`.

PR further explains the numerical/delay cause near `a == 1`: when `a` is close to 1, `1 / (a - 1)` is large; for sufficiently small `U`, `X` can be much larger than `RAND_INT_MAX` and may even overflow to infinity, increasing the time spent rejecting values that are too big.

The issue discussion notes an extremely long but finite expected delay: probability of drawing `0.0` means `1.0-draw` is 1 and “the rejection sampler will always exit”; “It may take an extraordinarily long time (1 in 2**53), but not a bug.”
Legacy implementation models a Zipf distribution truncated to signed long (`sys.maxint`) and rejects values where `X > (double)RAND_INT_MAX || X < 1.0` in a `while (1)` loop.
reproduction_risks: Reproducing a “hang” depends on random draws and may be very long/appear infinite; the issue notes it “may take an extraordinarily long time (1 in 2**53)”.
Behavior differs specifically for parameter `a` extremely close to 1 (e.g., `1.0000000000001`); using a different `a` may not trigger the issue.
Iteration count/stopping is implicit in the rejection loop (`while (1)` / repeated rejection); reproducer must run until a value is accepted rather than relying on a fixed iteration budget.
Stopping criteria and tolerance are not described in the passages; reproducer may need to observe acceptance rather than any convergence/tolerance-based termination.
